Rashi on Pesachim 65a:10:1.hebrew: ומנא ידע - רבי יהודה אם נתקבל בכלי? והא חששא בעלמא הוא דקאמר, שאם ישפך דמו. וכיון דלתקוני ספיקי אתא, היכי מיתקני בהכי? שמא לא נתקבל:
Rashi on Pesachim 65a:10:1.english: And how does [he] know - Rabbi Yehuda, whether it was received in a vessel? For he is merely stating a concern, that if its blood should spill [one collects it from the floor]. And since he comes to rectify cases of doubt, how are they rectified through this? Perhaps it was not received [in a vessel]!

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:10:2.hebrew: כהנים זריזין הן - וליכא למיחש לשמא לא קיבלוהו. לישנא אחרינא: שמא לא נתקבל בכלי כל זה שאתה שואב מארץ, ונמצאת זורק דם פסול? אף אני לא אמרתי למלאות אלא ממקום שיודעין שנשפכו שם דמים שנתקבלו בכלי. ואי משום דמיערב בהו מהאי דלא נתקבל, כגון דם התמצית — הא קא פריך ליה בסיפא. וראשון עיקר:
Rashi on Pesachim 65a:10:2.english: Priests are vigilant - and there is no need to be concerned that perhaps they did not receive it [in a vessel]. Another version: Perhaps all this [blood] that you scoop from the floor was not received in a vessel, and you end up sprinkling disqualified blood? [To this, he answers:] I too did not say to fill [the cup] except from a place where they know that blood that had been received in a vessel was spilled there. And if [you are concerned] that some of that which was not received, such as draining blood, is mixed with it — behold, [the Gemara] raises this objection against him at the end [of the passage]. And the first [explanation] is the primary one.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:10:3.hebrew: אי זריזין הן - היכן נשפכין? הא זריזין הן וידעי:
Rashi on Pesachim 65a:10:3.english: If they are vigilant - How did [the blood] spill? Behold, they are vigilant and know [to be careful].

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:10:4.hebrew: אגב זריזותייהו - שממהרים לרוץ ולקרב ולזרוק, מיתשיד מידייהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 65a:10:4.english: Owing to their speed - Because they hurry to run, to bring [the blood] near, and to sprinkle [it], [it] spills from their hands.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:11:1.hebrew: והלא דם התמצית - של פסחים הרבה מעורב בו, ואי נשפך דם של אחד כולו, בטל במיעוטו, ומה תועיל זריקה? שהרי בטל:
Rashi on Pesachim 65a:11:1.english: But isn't the residual blood - of many Paschal [offerings] mixed with it? And if all the blood of one [offering] was spilled, it is nullified in its minority, so what will sprinkling [the blood] avail, since it is nullified?

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:11:2.english: The draining blood - Of non-sacred [animals] and of consecrated [animals].

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:11:3.hebrew: באזהרה - בלאו ולא כרת, דכתיב: "כי נפש כל בשר דמו בנפשו הוא" וגו' עד "כל אוכליו יכרת" — יצא דם התמצית, שאינו דם הנפש. ובמסכת כריתות מפרש טעמא: חמשה לאוין כתיבי בדם, ומייתיר חד לדם התמצית:
Rashi on Pesachim 65a:11:3.english: A warning - [He violates] a negative prohibition, and not [a prohibition carrying the penalty of] karet, as it is written: "For the life of all flesh, its blood is in its life," etc., until "whoever eats it shall be cut off" — excluding the draining blood [dam hatamtitz], which is not the life-blood. And in Tractate Keritot [the Gemara] explains the reason: five negative prohibitions are written concerning blood, and one is superfluous [to apply] to the draining blood.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:12:1.english: With regard to atonement - [Meaning] that it is not fit for sprinkling.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:1:1.hebrew: ועולה גופה מנלן - שמתן דמה במקום שיש תחתיו יסוד, למעוטי מזרח ודרום, חוץ מאמה למזרח אצל צפון ואמה לדרום אצל מערב, דהכי תנן (מדות פ"ג מ"א): אוכל במזרח אמה אחת ובדרום אמה אחת:
Rashi on Pesachim 65a:1:1.english: And the burnt-offering itself, from where do we [derive it] - That the application of its blood [must be] in a place that has a base beneath it — to exclude the east and south [sides], except for one cubit on the east [side] next to the north and one cubit on the south [side] next to the west; for so we learned in the Mishnah (Middot 3:1): "[The base] extended on the east one cubit and on the south one cubit."

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:1:2.hebrew: אל יסוד מזבח העולה - גבי חטאת [נשיא] כתיב: ״ולקח הכהן מדם החטאת באצבעו ונתן על קרנות מזבח העולה ואת דמו ישפך אל יסוד מזבח העולה״. וה"ל למיכתב ״אל יסוד המזבח״, למה לי דכתיב ״מזבח העולה״? אלא הכי קאמר: אל יסוד מזבח תעשה העולה:
Rashi on Pesachim 65a:1:2.english: At the base of the altar of the burnt-offering - Regarding the sin-offering of a ruler, it is written: "And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin-offering with his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of the burnt-offering, and its blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of the burnt-offering." Now, it should have written "at the base of the altar"; why do I need [it to say] "the altar of the burnt-offering"? Rather, this is what it is saying: at the base of the altar, the burnt-offering shall be offered.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:2:1.english: Lazy - Because it acted lazily to be last.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:2:2.english: But it would not be sufficient without this - For [it is] a mitzvah [to have] three groups.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:3:1.english: To hurry themselves - To be among the first.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:4:1.hebrew: שלא ברצון רבי אליעזר - דאמר בעלמא גבי מכבד, דהיינו דומיא דהדחה, איכא חיוב חטאת. הלכך במקדש, כשכבר נעשה צורך גבוה, אסור:
Rashi on Pesachim 65a:4:1.english: Contrary to the wishes of Rabbi Eliezer - Who says elsewhere regarding sweeping [the floor], which is similar to rinsing [it], [that] there is liability for a sin-offering. Therefore, in the Temple, once the requirement of the Most High has already been fulfilled, it is prohibited.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:5:1.english: One who milks - [One who] draws the milk from the animal.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:5:2.hebrew: מחבץ - מעמיד החלב, ועושה ממנו חביצין שקורין מטונ"ש (גושים (של חלב חמוץ)):
Rashi on Pesachim 65a:5:2.english: Sets milk to curdle - [He] curdles the milk and makes curds from it, which are called matons (lumps (of sour milk)).

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:5:3.english: And one who removes [honeycombs] - As it is written (I Samuel 14:27): "and he dipped it in the honeycomb."

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:6:1.hebrew: אחד זה ואחד זה - מכבד ומרבץ ורודה, אבל מאידך לא קאמרי, דתולדות אב מלאכה נינהו, כדאמרינן בפרק המצניע. רבי אליעזר משום הכי מחייב — חולב משום מפרק, מגבן משום בונה, מחבץ משום בורר, בהמצניע — ומרבץ ומכבד מפרש התם משום אשוויי גומות:
Rashi on Pesachim 65a:6:1.english: Both this and that - [This refers to] sweeping, sprinkling [water on the floor], and detaching [honeycombs]; but regarding the other [actions] they do not say [this], for they are derivatives of primary categories of labor, as we say in chapter Hamatzni'a. Rabbi Eliezer holds [one] liable on account of this — milking on account of extracting [mefarek], making cheese on account of building [boneh], churning on account of selecting [borer], [as stated] in Hamatzni'a — and sprinkling and sweeping, it explains there, [he holds liable] on account of leveling hollows.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:7:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר - לעולם רבנן דאמרי בעלמא נמי שבות הוא, ומתני' כר' נתן, דאמר שבות שאינה צריכה לא התירו במקדש:
Rashi on Pesachim 65a:7:1.english: Rav Ashi said - Actually, [the Mishnah follows] the Rabbis, who say [that] elsewhere as well it is a rabbinic prohibition, and our Mishnah is in accordance with Rabbi Natan, who says [that] a rabbinic prohibition that is not necessary was not permitted in the Temple.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:8:1.english: That if the blood of one of them was spilled - onto the ground, and [none] of it was sprinkled on the altar.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:8:2.english: This cup is found to render it fit - For [some] of the spilled [blood] is mixed into it.

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:9:1.hebrew: שמא לא נתקבל בכלי - אותו שאתה רוצה להכשיר, שמא לא נתקבל בכלי, ותו לא מהניא ליה זריקה, דתנן: נשפך מצואר בהמה על הרצפה ואספו — פסול, בזבחים בפרק שני (דף טו.):
Rashi on Pesachim 65a:9:1.english: Perhaps it had not been received in a vessel - That [blood] which you wish to validate — perhaps it had not been received in a vessel, and throwing [the blood] is no longer effective for it, as we learned in a Mishnah: "[If blood] spilled from the neck of an animal onto the floor and one gathered it, [it is] disqualified," in Zevachim, in the second chapter (15a).

Rashi on Pesachim 65a:9:2.english: I, too, did not say - that it is effective, except when it was received in a vessel.

Tosafot on Pesachim 65a:5:1.hebrew: החולב כגרוגרות - הקשה ה"ר אפרים, דתנן בפ' המוציא (שבת עו:) דשיעור המוציא חלב כדי גמיאה, ושיעורי שבת הן שוים לכל המלאכות — הוצאה, טחינה וקצירה. ותירץ, דסתם חלב כדי גמיאה, שהוא שיעור גדול; אבל הכא בחולב לגבינה, דאחשובי אחשביה, שיעורו כגרוגרות דזוטר. אבל אי כדי גמיאה זוטר, צריך לומר דסתם חלב לגבינה, ולכך הכא שיעורו כגרוגרת, והא דמיחייב בכדי גמיאה היינו במפרש בהדיא לאכילה ולשתיה; דאי סתם חולב לאכילה ולשתיה ולא לגבינ', אפילו היה מפרש בהדיא לגבינה היה לו להתחייב בכדי גמיאה דזוטר, הואיל וסתמו לאכול ולשתות, כדאמרינן בסוף כלל גדול (שבת עו.): "המוציא תבן כמלא פי פרה לגמל — חייב", אף על גב דלגמל לא הוי שיעורא בהכי, הואיל וסתמא לפרה — מיחייב אשיעורא דפרה. ויש מפרש, דכשהחלב כבר בעין מיחייב בכדי גמיאה, אבל חולב לא מיחייב אלא בכגרוגרת, דאין אדם טורח לחלוב בפחות מגרוגרת; וכי האי גוונא מפליג בהמוציא (שבת עט.) גבי עור לעשות קמיע:
Tosafot on Pesachim 65a:5:1.english: One who milks — [in the measure of] a dried fig-bulk - Rabbi Ephraim raised a difficulty, for we learned in a Mishnah in chapter HaMotzi (Shabbat 76b) that the measure [for liability] of one who carries out milk [on Shabbat] is enough for a swallow, and the Shabbat measures are equal for all labors — carrying out, grinding, and reaping. And he answered that ordinarily milk [has the measure of] enough for a swallow, which is a large measure; but here [our baraita] is speaking of one who milks [with the intention] to make cheese, where he gives it significance [even in a smaller amount], [so] its measure is a dried fig-bulk, which is smaller. However, if [the measure of] enough for a swallow is smaller [than a dried fig-bulk], one must say that ordinarily milk is [intended] for cheese, and therefore here [in the baraita] its measure is a dried fig-bulk, whereas that [Mishnah] where one is liable for enough for a swallow refers to where he explicitly specifies [that it is] for eating and drinking; for if ordinarily one who milks does so for eating and drinking and not for cheese, even if he had explicitly specified [that he was milking] for cheese, he should be liable for enough for a swallow, which is smaller, since its ordinary use is for eating and drinking, as we say at the end of [chapter] Klal Gadol (Shabbat 76a): "One who carries out straw [in the measure of] a cow's mouthful for a camel is liable" — even though for a camel that is not a [sufficient] measure, since it is ordinarily for a cow, he is liable according to the measure of a cow. And there are those who explain that when the milk is already extant [i.e., already milked], one is liable [for carrying it out] in [the measure of] enough for a swallow, whereas one who milks is liable only for a dried fig-bulk, because a person does not trouble himself to milk less than a dried fig-bulk; and in a similar manner [the Gemara] distinguishes in [chapter] HaMotzi (Shabbat 79a) regarding hide [used] to make an amulet.

Tosafot on Pesachim 65a:5:2.hebrew: המכבד והמרבץ - ע"כ לאו פסיק רישיה הוא, דבפסיק רישיה לא הוה שרי ר"ש לרבץ לכתחלה בשילהי המצניע (שבת צה.). ותימה לר"י, דא"כ אמאי מחייב רבי אליעזר כיון דיכול להיות בלא גומות? ודוחק לומר דפליגי אי הוי פסיק רישיה אי לא. ונראה לר"י דבהא פליגי: דר' אליעזר סבר סתם מכבד ומרבץ מתכוון להשוות גומות — אף על פי שא"צ להשוות גומות, מיחייב לרבי יהודה הואיל והשוה גומות לבסוף; ורבנן סברי דאין מתכוון אלא לכבד ולרבץ בעלמא, וליכא אלא שבות. תימה לר"י: היכי מתוקמא מתניתין כרבי אליעזר? והא בעזרה, שהיה לה רצפת אבנים, לא שייך בה אשוויי גומות, ואפילו לכתחלה שרי, כדאמר בשילהי המצניע (גם זה שם): אמימר שרא זילחא במחוזא; אע"ג דגזרינן בבמה מדליקין (שבת דף כט:) עיליתא דשישא אטו עיליתא דעלמא, מחוזא היתה כולה רצופה באבנים — לא גזרינן אטו דעיר דעלמא! ואור"י דבעזרה בין רובד לרובד היו גומות. אי נמי, דלרבי אליעזר, דאיכא איסורא דאורייתא בכיבוד דעלמא, גזרינן עזרה אטו כיבוד דעלמא, דכמה שבות אשכחן במקדש בפ' בתרא דעירובין (דף קב:); אבל לרבנן, דאפילו בעלמא ליכא אלא איסורא דרבנן, אין שבות כי האי במקדש, כיון דליכא איסורא דאוריית' בשום מקום. פסק בהלכות גדולות דכיבוד מותר, כדאמרינן בהמצניע (דף צה.) גבי ריבוץ: האידנא קיימא לן כרבי שמעון דשרי לרבץ לכתחלה. ואין נראה לר"י, דהא מזיז עפר ממקומו אסרינן בכירה (שבת דף לט.) ובביצה (ד' ח.). ועוד, בפרק כל הכלים (שבת דף קכד:) אמרינן: "אמר רבי (אליעזר) אף מכבדות של תמרה מותר לטלטל", ופריך: "אי מחמה לצל, בהא לימא רבי (אליעזר) כו'", משמע דפשיטא דהוי מלאכתו לאיסור לכולי עלמא. ואף על גב דריבוץ שרי לכתחלה לרבי שמעון, בכיבוד אסור, דמשוי ביה גומות יותר מריבוץ:
Tosafot on Pesachim 65a:5:2.english: One who sweeps and one who sprinkles - Perforce, this is not an inevitable consequence [pesik reishei], for if it were an inevitable consequence, Rabbi Shimon would not have permitted sprinkling initially [lekhatchilah] at the end of [chapter] Hamatzni'a (Shabbat 95a). And it is astonishing to R"i: for if so, why does Rabbi Eliezer hold [him] liable, since it can happen without [leveling] hollows? And it is forced to say that they disagree as to whether it is an inevitable consequence or not. And it appears to R"i that they disagree about this: Rabbi Eliezer holds that an ordinary person who sweeps or sprinkles intends to level hollows — even though he does not need to level hollows, he is liable according to Rabbi Yehudah since he leveled hollows in the end; whereas the Rabbis hold that he intends only to sweep and sprinkle generally, and there is only a rabbinic prohibition [shevut]. It is astonishing to R"i: how can our Mishnah be established in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer? For in the Temple courtyard, which had a stone floor, leveling hollows does not apply to it, and it should be permitted even initially, as [the Gemara] says at the end of Hamatzni'a (ibid.): Ameimar permitted sprinkling in Mechoza; even though we decree in [chapter] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 29b) [regarding] a marble upper room on account of an ordinary upper room, [since] Mechoza was entirely paved with stones, we do not decree [there] on account of an ordinary city! And R"i says that in the Temple courtyard, between one stone pavement and another, there were hollows. Alternatively, according to Rabbi Eliezer, since there is a Torah prohibition in ordinary sweeping, we decree [against sweeping in] the Temple courtyard on account of ordinary sweeping, for we find several rabbinic prohibitions [shevut] in the Temple in the last chapter of Eruvin (102b); however, according to the Rabbis, since even in general there is only a rabbinic prohibition, there is no such rabbinic prohibition in the Temple, since there is no Torah prohibition anywhere [in this act]. It is ruled in Halakhot Gedolot that sweeping is permitted, as we say in Hamatzni'a (95a) regarding sprinkling: nowadays we hold like Rabbi Shimon, who permits sprinkling initially. But this does not appear [correct] to R"i, for we prohibit moving earth from its place in [chapter] Kirah (Shabbat 39a) and in Beitzah (8a). And furthermore, in chapter Kol HaKelim (Shabbat 124b) we say: "Rabbi (Eliezer) said: Even brooms of palm branches are permitted to be moved," and [the Gemara] asks: "If [it is moved] from the sun to the shade, would Rabbi (Eliezer) say in this [case], etc.?" — which implies that it is obvious that it is [a utensil whose] function is for a prohibited act according to everyone. And even though sprinkling is permitted initially according to Rabbi Shimon, sweeping is prohibited, because one levels hollows with it more than with sprinkling.

Tosafot on Pesachim 65a:9:1.hebrew: שמא לא נתקבל בכלי - פי' בקונטרס: ולא תועיל זריקה, משום דנשפך מצואר בהמה. וקשה לר"י, דמ"מ יזרוק, דתועיל זריקה לאותו שנשפך אחר שנתקבל! ונראה לר"י, דהכי פי': "שמא לא נתקבל בכלי", ואסור להעלות דם פסול על גבי המזבח, כדמוכח בכמה דוכתי, דדוקא אם עלו בדיעבד — לא ירדו; וקאמר: "אף אני לא אמרתי אלא בנתקבל", דסמכינן אזריזות כהנים, כדמסיק. ודוקא מדם הראוי להתקבל פריך; אבל דם התמצית כמים בעלמא חשיב — כיון דאינו ראוי לכיסוי, אינו אוסר להעלותו. וכי פריך "והלא דם התמצית מעורב בו ומבטיל ליה ברוב", לא פריך מדם הראוי להתקבל ונשפך, דעולין אין מבטלין זה את זה אפי' לרבנן, כדאמר בהקומץ רבה (מנחות דף כב:):
Tosafot on Pesachim 65a:9:1.english: "Perhaps it was not received in a vessel" - Rashi explained: and sprinkling will not be effective, because it spilled from the neck of the animal [onto the floor]. And it is difficult for Ri: nevertheless, let him sprinkle [from the mixed blood], for the sprinkling will be effective for that [blood] which spilled after it had been received [in a vessel]! And it appears to Ri that this is its explanation: "Perhaps it was not received in a vessel," and it is forbidden to bring unfit blood up onto the altar, as is proven in several places, for it is only if they were brought up after the fact (bedi'avad) that they do not come down; and [Rabbi Yehuda] says: "I, too, spoke only about [blood] that had been received [in a vessel]," for we rely on the vigilance of the priests, as [the Gemara] concludes. And specifically regarding blood that is fit to be received does [the Gemara] ask [this]; however, dam hatamtzit [blood that drains out after the initial spurt] is considered like mere water — since it is not fit for covering [the blood], it does not forbid bringing it [the mixture] up [onto the altar]. And when [the Gemara later] asks, "But isn't dam hatamtzit mixed with it, and it nullifies it in a majority?" it does not ask regarding blood that was fit to be received and spilled [onto the floor], because [sacrificial substances that] go up [onto the altar] (olin) do not nullify one another, even according to the Rabbis, as is stated in [the chapter] HaKometz Rabbah (Menachot 22b).
